nodes.description: Public constant role hash keccak256("MANAGER_ROLE") used to gate privileged token locking and minting operations.
Public constant keccak256("MintableERC20") token type identifier declared but not referenced by any logic in this contract.
Public constant keccak256("Transfer(address,address,uint256)") used to validate the exit log topic0 signature.
Boolean initializer guard inherited from Initializable that prevents repeated initialize() calls.
Empty public constructor of MintableERC20Predicate; performs no role or owner setup.
External initializer that sets the contract id and grants DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and MANAGER_ROLE to the supplied owner address.
External only(MANAGER_ROLE) entry point that decodes the deposit amount and performs a safeTransferFrom of root tokens into the predicate.
Public only(MANAGER_ROLE) exit handler that parses the child-chain burn log, validates the Transfer topic0/from/to fields, mints missing tokens if needed and transfers the amount to the withdrawer.
Caller identity read via _msgSender(); used as the subject of the only(MANAGER_ROLE) role check in privileged functions.
External IERC20(rootToken).safeTransferFrom call executed inside lockTokens, wrapping a low-level call to an arbitrary token address.
External IERC20(rootToken).safeTransfer call executed inside exitTokens, sending the computed amount to the withdrawer address.
External IMintableERC20(rootToken).mint call executed inside exitTokens when the predicate balance is insufficient, minting amount - tokenBalance to the predicate.
Low-level target.call{value:...}(data) invoked by Address.functionCall/_callOptionalReturn underlying SafeERC20 transfers, handing control to the token contract.
Address argument of initialize() that receives DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and MANAGER_ROLE.
Address argument of lockTokens() from which the root tokens are pulled.
Address argument of lockTokens() representing the child-chain recipient; only emitted in the LockedMintableERC20 event.
Address argument of lockTokens() identifying the ERC20 token that is transferred into the predicate.
Raw bytes argument of lockTokens() that is ABI-decoded into the deposit amount.
Address argument of exitTokens() identifying the token that is minted/transferred on exit.
RLP-encoded bytes argument of exitTokens() describing the child-chain burn receipt log.
Local uint256 decoded from depositData in lockTokens() and passed to safeTransferFrom.
Local address derived from log topic1 (from) in exitTokens() and used as the safeTransfer recipient.
Local uint256 holding token.balanceOf(address(this)) in exitTokens(), compared against the exit amount.
Local uint256 decoded from logRLPList[2] in exitTokens(), used for the mint shortfall and the final safeTransfer.

edges.reason: initialize() is callable by any external caller (msg.sender) protected only by the initializer guard, so the first caller can seize DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and MANAGER_ROLE via _owner.
lockTokens() is gated by the only(MANAGER_ROLE) modifier which evaluates hasRole(role, _msgSender()), so msg.sender controls whether the privileged token pull executes.
exitTokens() is gated by the only(MANAGER_ROLE) modifier which checks _msgSender() against the role set before parsing the log and minting/transferring.
The _owner parameter flows into _setupRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE) and _setupRole(MANAGER_ROLE), permanently granting privileged roles to caller-supplied address.
The inherited inited flag gates the initializer modifier: require(!inited) allows a single initialize() execution before inited is set true.
MANAGER_ROLE is the role argument of the only modifier protecting lockTokens().
MANAGER_ROLE is the role argument of the only modifier protecting exitTokens().
TRANSFER_EVENT_SIG is compared against logTopicRLPList[0].toUint() to validate that the exit log is a Transfer event.
The attacker/managers-supplied RLP log bytes are parsed via toRlpItem().toList() inside exitTokens().
log topic1 is decoded into the withdrawer address, meaning the destination of the transfer is derived from the supplied log.
logRLPList[2] is decoded into the exit amount, meaning the minted/transferred quantity is derived from the supplied log.
The rootToken parameter of exitTokens() is cast to IMintableERC20 and used for balanceOf, mint and safeTransfer.
depositData is abi.decode'd into the local amount that is forwarded to safeTransferFrom.
The depositor parameter becomes the 'from' argument of IERC20(rootToken).safeTransferFrom inside lockTokens().
The decoded amount local variable becomes the 'value' argument of IERC20(rootToken).safeTransferFrom.
The caller-supplied rootToken address is the target of the external safeTransferFrom call, allowing an arbitrary token contract to be invoked.
rootToken is cast to IERC20 and used as the call target for the token interaction initiated from lockTokens() context.
Execution reaches the safeTransferFrom external call only after the only(MANAGER_ROLE) check and the event emission in lockTokens().
exitTokens() conditionally calls token.mint(address(this), amount - tokenBalance) when the predicate balance is insufficient.
The tokenBalance < amount comparison determines whether the mint shortfall branch is taken.
amount - tokenBalance computes the mint shortfall; this subtraction is guarded by the tokenBalance < amount branch, mapping overflow/underflow risk to arithmetic.
The caller-supplied rootToken is cast to IMintableERC20 and targeted by the privileged mint call.
The log-derived withdrawer address becomes the recipient of IERC20(rootToken).safeTransfer.
The log-derived amount becomes the value moved by IERC20(rootToken).safeTransfer.
The caller-supplied rootToken is the call target of the final safeTransfer in exitTokens().
The final safeTransfer executes at the end of exitTokens() after signature, recipient and balance checks.
safeTransferFrom resolves to _callOptionalReturn -> Address.functionCall -> target.call, transferring control to the token contract which may re-enter lockTokens().
safeTransfer resolves to a low-level target.call, giving the token contract control before the transaction completes, enabling reentrant state manipulation.
The mint call is an external call to the token contract that can re-enter the predicate while tokenBalance/amount accounting is still in flight.

normalization_plan.reason: _owner is used only to assign roles inside initialize() and has no independent identity; it should be folded into the initialize function node.
depositor is a transient input consumed solely by the lockTokens safeTransferFrom call.
depositReceiver only appears in the LockedMintableERC20 event inside lockTokens and carries no independent flow.
The lockTokens rootToken parameter directly selects the target contract of the safeTransferFrom external call.
depositData is raw calldata immediately decoded into the local amount inside lockTokens.
The decoded amount is only meaningful as the value argument of the safeTransferFrom call.
The exitTokens rootToken parameter is the call target of the closing safeTransfer/mint sequence.
log is the RLP input parsed entirely within exitTokens to derive withdrawer and amount.
withdrawer exists only to serve as the recipient of the safeTransfer call.
tokenBalance is read only to decide and size the conditional mint call.
The log-derived amount is used only as the value of the mint shortfall and the final safeTransfer.
